title: bug: under MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1 on Windows, npm .cmd shims (claude.cmd, codex.cmd) and cmd.exe search the project directory before PATH, so a project-root node.exe still runs
description:
Found by CQ-RF07 (task-f3f364a6), the epic-final adversarial review. It is residual 3 in architect-54e5eb09's comment-1deae51a on that row, and task-64809b19 does not fix it.

Evidence at 28df02f7: moe-agent.ps1 pins node (Find-MoeProtectedFile, MOE_PROTECTED_INTERPRETER_NOT_FOUND) and resolves the agent CLI to an absolute path outside the project. But the seat runs with the project as its working directory, and the resolved CLI is typically an npm shim (`claude.cmd`) that runs `node` by bare name when no node.exe sits beside it. cmd.exe, and CreateProcess without NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath, look in the current directory before PATH. A repository that ships `node.exe` at its root therefore runs it inside the protected seat, whatever PATH order the wrapper sets.

Fix direction: under the marker, set NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath=1 in the environment the wrapper gives the CLI (cmd.exe and CreateProcess both honour it), or run a resolved .cmd CLI through the pinned node directly. Pin the behaviour with a ps1 row that plants <project>\node.exe and asserts it never runs.
definitionOfDone: Under MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1 on Windows, a node.exe (or other bare-named helper) planted at the project root never runs through the agent CLI's shim or any cmd.exe child of the seat; a postflight or node --test row on Windows node.exe proves it with a planted file.
Legacy seats are unchanged, and the sh/ps1 parity check passes.
The protected-agent-command and launcher suites exit 0 on Linux and through Windows node.exe.

implementationPlan.description:
The fix: one line per twin, right after the marker is read (DoD 1 and 2). Use an editor tool.

- The exact hunks are in /mnt/d/moe-scratch/2f22237b-plan/ps1.diff and sh.diff.

scripts/moe-agent.ps1, directly after `$script:MoeRuntimeProtected = ($env:MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED -ceq '1')` (:469 at a0269bcd):
# cmd.exe, which runs an npm .cmd shim such as claude.cmd, looks a bare name up in
# the current directory (the project) before PATH unless this is set; every child
# inherits it. Node's own spawn of a bare name ignores it. Same line in moe-agent.sh.
if ($script:MoeRuntimeProtected) { $env:NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath = '1' }

scripts/moe-agent.sh, directly after `if [ "${MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED:-}" = 1 ]; then RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1; else RUNTIME_PROTECTED=0; fi` (:51): the same three comment lines, ending 'Same line in moe-agent.ps1.', then
if [ "$RUNTIME_PROTECTED" = 1 ]; then export NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath=1; fi

Why here:
- This is the earliest point that knows the marker, before any child process. The CLI inherits it (PowerShell runs a .cmd CLI through cmd.exe, from Invoke-MoeGuardedCommand), and so does every other child.
- cmd.exe honours the variable. On Linux and macOS it is inert.
- Legacy (marker unset, or not exactly '1') never sets it and never clears an inherited value.
- Under Git Bash, Cygwin also runs a .cmd CLI through cmd.exe, so the sh line covers that seat. The suite cannot run Git Bash rows; its own comment says why.

Error handling: an env assignment cannot fail, and nothing new can refuse or exit. No new MOE_ code, so parity-check.sh needs no new literal.

Re-run C1 and C2: both must pass.

comments.author: worker-c9368191
comments.content:
Planner input from CQ-RF07 (task-f3f364a6), epic-final review, finding 6 (LOW, Windows ps1, same class as this row).

`Find-MoeProtectedFile` (scripts/moe-agent.ps1 ~499-523) skips in-project PATH entries by comparing `Get-MoeRealPath` strings (`$real.Equals($project)` or the `"$real$sep".StartsWith("$project$sep")` check at ~518). It compares spellings, not file identity, so the same folder reached through an 8.3 short name, a `subst` drive or a `\\?\`/UNC spelling slips past the containment check, and a node.exe there would be pinned. The JetBrains side matches by file identity (task-9a1da6f6).

This needs the user's own PATH to carry such an alias of the project, which is why it is LOW. Fold an identity compare (volume serial plus file index, as the plugin does), or an explicit refusal of 8.3/subst/UNC entries, into this row's Windows fix, with a postflight.ps1 row.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: 1) Export NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath=1 under the marker in both twins, CHOSEN. It is one line each. cmd.exe honours it, so it closes the npm .cmd shim and every cmd.exe child, and it is inert elsewhere. 2) Run a resolved .cmd CLI through the pinned node directly (parse the shim's JS entry). Rejected: it parses third-party shim text per CLI (claude, codex, gemini, grok), and it still leaves the CLI's own cmd.exe children exposed. 3) Run the CLI with a cwd outside the project. planningNotes.codebaseInsights: In this suite's fixture, worker rows never launch a CLI: the inert runtime answers no claim, so they stop at MOE_TASKLESS_NO_LAUNCH reason=claim-failed. A governor seat synthesizes hasNext:false and launches its CLI, which makes it the cheap way to observe the CLI's environment through the real launcher. On Windows the launch first runs the agent Git guard, whose Node program spawns git, so a row that reaches the CLI needs git on PATH. Planning probes on native Windows showed, for PS 5.1 and PS 7: at HEAD under the marker, the trusted claude.cmd shim ran <project>\node.exe; with the line set, it runs the PATH node, and legacy still runs the planted copy.
